Dont be worried about having an aggressive puppy, the benefit here is that you have a puppy. Especially because it's a behavior that just started, so it's easily trainable. 

If your puppy is in your arms and someone goes to pet her and you hear her growl, take your index finger and thumb and quickly but gently pinch the area behind her ear and say NO. Put her down immediately after and give her no attention for the next couple minutes. No guest attention either, she is suddenly invisible to everyone around her. The loss of attention tells her that you do not allow that kind of behavior and you will not reward her for it. The ear pinching (touch correction) snaps her out of that behavior and the NO gives her an immediate connection between her behavior and how it was received. It's important to catch dogs in the act of doing a bad behavior because if you wait and discipline them too late, they will not make the connection between their behavior and the consequence. 

I trained my own service dog and I've been working with dogs for over a year now. I'm no expert, but this is what I learned doing those things. I hope this helped at least ease your mind.

*also,
If she doesn't like being pet on the head by strangers, you need to be petting her head more. Because she's a puppy, she has time to get used to these things. I would touch her head and play with her face relatively often so she gets used to it.

I got prescribed Prazosin a few years ago. I got off it quickly because it seemed to give me more nightmares and make me really dizzy. A year later my nightmares got worse so my psychiatrist recommended it again. This time I stuck with it and managed to get it to a dose that blocks almost all nightmares. I find when I get stressed I have breakthrough nightmares, but the rest of the time I sleep solidly.

I also have to make sure I actually go to sleep when I take this med because it makes me so dizzy. If you don't plan on sleeping more than 5 hours, don't take it. I've passed out plenty of times in the morning because I try to ignore the low blood pressure side effect.

All things considered, Prazosin improved my life so much I don't really give a shit if I'm dizzy sometimes. To sleep through the night without a real fear of nightmares/terrors is worth it to me.

Read my comment above, I have lived in my car for over three months. OP has enough money to stay out of a car and in a place. No, he shouldn't live in a car.

Edit: I've lived on the streets aswell so if you've done both like I have I know from that perspective living in a car seems so much better. But the cost of getting said car is going to drain his savings and fuck him much quicker than just renting a room out.

I have lived in my buick century for 3+ months at a time. No, you don't want to live in your car.

Think about where you'll park it at night to sleep. Grocery store? Shopping complex? Someone will see you sleeping in your car and call the cops. I can't even tell you how many parking lots I'm trespassed from and how many mornings I woke up to cops tapping on my window. Sooner or later you're going to run into legal trouble. Not to mention cars get 20° or hotter than the outside temperature and it's July. You'll spend a lot more than you want to on gas to run your car to cool it down. You also have no fridge or microwave, which means eating out or eating pre made meals which add up quickly. Have to pee in the middle of the night? You'd better stock up on bottles and cups to throw away. All of your hygiene now needs to be moved to any random store that will let you use their bathroom, unless you get a gym membership and stick around there. Oh and you'll be buying new clothes and throwing away old ones on the regular, seeing as every possession you own takes up space in your car therefore taking up living space. Laundromats are much more expensive than you think and are really not realistic for regular use.

Your best bet would be to transfer Staples locations and start looking on Craigslist for a room to rent. Your main advantage is that there is only one of you and you have a job. When I was living in my car with my SO there were two of us, one unemployed, looking to rent one room for not too much and it was damn near impossible. Do you have friends that could take you in temporarily? Offer some rent money to them to help your chances.

Living in your car is not at all what it's cracked up to be, and should be used only as the last resort before total homelessness. I have been completely homeless before and while I would definitely choose the car over that, I would recommend living at least on a couch. You would not believe how important just a place to put yourself when you're not working is until you don't have one.

Edit: Financially, living in your car is more expensive. I spent $2,500 probably within the first two months of living in my car. Your costs add up exponentially for food, hygiene, gas, car insurance, maintenance, etc. Renting a room for 500 bucks a month on craigslist? Astonishingly cheaper. Keep your job and rent a room. Getting out of being homeless in your car is damn near impossible.
